candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method printFailures to class TextListener
candidates.description:
Move method printFailures to org.junit.internal.TextListener
Rationale: The method printFailures() is responsible for printing the results of test failures, which directly relates to the functionality of the TextListener class. This class is designed to handle output related to test results, including the printing of failures. Moving this method to TextListener aligns with the Single Responsibility Principle, as it centralizes all failure reporting logic within the class that manages output. Additionally, since the method utilizes the getWriter() method from TextListener to print messages, it makes sense for it to reside within the same class to maintain cohesion and reduce dependencies on external classes.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method printFooter to class TextListener
candidates.description:
Move method printFooter to org.junit.internal.TextListener
Rationale: The printFooter() method is responsible for outputting the results of a test run, including success and failure messages. Since TextListener is already handling the output through its PrintStream (fWriter), it is logical to move this method to TextListener. This will encapsulate all output-related functionality within the TextListener class, adhering to the Single Responsibility Principle. Additionally, the method directly interacts with the TextListener's writer, making it more cohesive to have it within the same class.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method printFooter to class ResultPrinter
candidates.description:
Move method printFooter to junit.textui.ResultPrinter
Rationale: The printFooter() method is responsible for printing the results of test executions, including success and failure messages. Moving printFooter() to ResultPrinter will enhance cohesion, as it will centralize all result-related printing logic within the ResultPrinter class. This change will also improve maintainability, as any future modifications to how results are printed can be made in one place, rather than scattered across multiple classes.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method runProtected to class Protectable
candidates.description:
Move method runProtected to junit.framework.Protectable
Rationale: The method runProtected() is designed to execute a Protectable instance's protect() method while handling various exceptions that may arise during its execution. Since the primary purpose of this method is to manage the execution of Protectable instances, it logically belongs to the Protectable class. Moving it there would encapsulate the behavior of running a Protectable and handling its exceptions, aligning with the interface's intent of providing a mechanism to run code that can throw exceptions.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method run to class TestCase
candidates.description:
Move method run to junit.framework.TestCase
Rationale: The method 'run(final TestCase test)' is designed to execute a test case, which directly aligns with the responsibilities of the TestCase class. This method encapsulates the logic for starting and ending a test, as well as handling the execution of the test itself through the 'runBare()' method. Since the TestCase class is responsible for defining and running test cases, it is logical to move this method there to maintain cohesion and ensure that all test-related functionalities are centralized within the TestCase class.

The Test class is responsible for running tests and managing their results, so it is logical for it to also handle the notification of test completion to listeners.

Moving this method to the Test class would encapsulate the behavior related to starting a test within the Test itself, promoting better cohesion and making it clearer that this functionality is part of the test's lifecycle management.

candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method evaluate2 to class ExpectException
candidates.description:
Move method evaluate2 to org.junit.internal.runners.statements.ExpectException
Rationale: The method evaluate2() is designed to handle the evaluation of exceptions in a testing context, specifically checking if the expected exception matches the thrown exception. Since the method directly interacts with the ExpectException class's properties, such as fExpected, it is logical to move it to this class. This will encapsulate the exception evaluation logic within the context of the ExpectException class, enhancing cohesion and making the code easier to maintain and understand.

Rationale: The method addFields() is closely related to the functionality of the AllMembersSupplier class, which is responsible for supplying parameters based on the public members of a target class. candidates.refactoringInfo: Move method filter2 to class JUnit38ClassRunner
candidates.description:
Move method filter2 to org.junit.internal.runners.JUnit38ClassRunner
Rationale: The method filter2() is closely related to the functionality of the JUnit38ClassRunner class, as it directly manipulates the test instances that the runner is responsible for. The method checks if the test is an instance of Filterable or TestSuite, which are both types of tests that the JUnit38ClassRunner would handle. Moving this method to JUnit38ClassRunner enhances cohesion by keeping filtering logic within the class that manages the execution of tests. Additionally, it allows for better encapsulation of the filtering behavior, making it easier to maintain and understand the relationship between the runner and the tests it executes.
